spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The module is the organizing map: the product of local absolute values descends to the semilocal quotient, relates its additive-measure L2 space to the multiplicative idele-class L2 space, and separates scaling from the kernel of the module. Taking kernel invariants then turns the general trace formula into the specialized form used earlier.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the semilocal ring A_S and quotient Y_S=A_S/Gamma, the product of local absolute values descends to Mod_S:Y_S->R_+*. The semilocal idele class group C_S acts by multiplication and embeds into Y_S as the orbit of 1; its complement has additive Haar measure zero. A Radon-Nikodym derivative yields a unitary identification w_S:L2(Y_S)->L2(C_S). The modulated group C_S is noncanonically isomorphic to R_+* x K_S, where K_S=ker Mod_S, and equation (22) is described as the K_S-invariant specialization of a general trace formula.
directed.conceptual_reading: The module records precisely how multiplicative motion rescales additive Haar measure. That correction makes the additive quotient and multiplicative orbit interchangeable at the Hilbert-space level up to null sets, while K_S-invariance removes norm-one directions and retains the scaling coordinate relevant to the specialized trace formula.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from local fields and their product norms to the quotient module, then from the full-measure idele-class orbit through a Radon-Nikodym unitary to L2(C_S), and finally through K_S invariants to the semilocal trace-formula interface.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The orbit embedding is only full measure, not equality of Y_S with C_S, and the product decomposition is explicitly noncanonical. This machinery specializes an existing trace formula; it is not an independent positivity theorem and does not supply the missing RH-critical estimate.
directed.uncertainty: Dense notation is partly degraded, equation (22) and the cited general trace formula are outside this packet, and the unit reports rather than derives the unitary identification. The maps, null-set qualification, and invariant specialization are nonetheless explicit.

supported: The candidate accurately records that the product module descends to the semilocal quotient, that the idele-class orbit embeds with measure-zero complement, and that a Radon-Nikodym derivative yields the stated unitary L2 identification.
It preserves the explicit noncanonicity of the product decomposition of the idele class group and identifies K_S as the kernel of the module.
It correctly states that equation (22) is presented as the K_S-invariant specialization of a cited general trace formula and does not turn the full-measure orbit into literal equality of spaces.
inference: Interpreting the module as the scaling coordinate and K_S invariance as discarding norm-one directions is a reasonable structural reading of the kernel and noncanonical product decomposition.
Describing the full-measure orbit and Radon-Nikodym unitary as a Hilbert-space interface between additive and multiplicative presentations is well supported.
